newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Right-wing bomber appears in S.African court.
newsitem.headline: Right-wing bomber appears in S.African court.

text.p: A right-wing bomber on the run for a year appeared in court on Tuesday after being caught after a new series of blasts which killed four blacks in South Africa.

Jan de Wet was convicted of murder in absentia a year ago after breaking out of jail while on trial for bombings which killed 20 people on the eve of South Africa's historic all-race elections in April 1994.
Police redoubled their hunt for him after two pipe bombs killed four blacks in the town of Worcester near Cape Town on Christmas Eve. He was arrested on Monday on a farm west of Johannesburg.

De Wet is to be questioned in connection with the Worcester blasts, but has only been charged with escaping from custody. He appeared in court briefly on Tuesday and was ordered to reappear on January 28.

De Wet was one of four members of the neo-Nazi Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB) who escaped from custody shortly before nine co-defendants were each sentenced to 26 years in jail for the pre-election bombings in and around Johannesburg.

A telephone caller claiming to represent the previously unknown Boere Attack Troops (BAT) told state television on Sunday night the group was responsible for the Worcester attacks as well as three bombings on Sunday in North West province.
The caller said his group was opposed to Moslems and communists because they rejected Christianity.
North West provincial Premier Popo Molefe said he believed militant right-wingers were renewing their efforts to destabilise the country.

"I do believe that there is a small group that is organised and is using commercial explosives to create a state of fear and panic," he told Reuters, adding that he was convinced that the vast majority of South Africans did not support their actions.
